sections.overall: A less eventful week than the previous one! But still plenty happening with the ratings, as always! Match of the week was Kyle Fletcher vs Komander (8.17) for the International Title. It was the latter's best singles match since 2023! It also was a boost to this title's rating , consolidating its status as the second most prestigious one currently in AEW.
sections.mens: No other exceptional Men's matches this week, the next best being Kevin Knight vs AR Fox (7.25) for the TNT title. Two top performers (Darby Allin and Will Ospreay) and underwhelming respective matches, which has knocked back their ratings somewhat. The first time an Ospreay match has been rated the lowest one on a show, and for all singles matches across a whole week (6.51).
sections.womens: Two great women's matches this week; each 7+ rated and both main eventing! Hikaru Shida continues her TBS title reign in her hard-hitting match against Queen Aminata. The Trios main event on Dynamite furthered several stories and feuds all in one go.
sections.menstag: Again, limited exposure for the Men's Tag division. The title match between Cage & Copeland and Garcia & Wheeler underwhelmed (5.52). Hopefully we'll see a better match from the champs at Redemption.
sections.womenstag: Although it wasn't technically a tag team match, both Divine Dominion and Hyan & World featured, so some gains there. With a tag title match scheduled next week, things could be picking up for the division.
sections.trios: As with last week, no Trios matches. Though there were some backstage developments so let's hope we don't see more teams drop out of the rankings each week.
